recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source edit is needed for FHIR-24871 unless the Financial Management work group later chooses to revise Claim.prescription beyond the Published R5 wording.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Claim issue requesting Claim.prescription to define a prescription as the document or authorization given to the claim author to provide reimbursable products and services, with examples such as medication prescriptions and orders for oxygen, wheelchairs, or physiotherapy.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentions FHIR-24871, but commit f952b5321de9cdbcb7b2521862890c757e21d530 changed Claim.prescription from the older pharmacy/device/vision-focused definition to the requested document/authorization wording. Current blame for the Claim.prescription definition points to that commit.
additional_context: Claim is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/claim/structuredefinition-Claim.xml is in build scope. Jira and community searches found no Zulip or Confluence record that changes the conclusion. Related FHIR-37910 requested the same wording for ExplanationOfBenefit.prescription, and the current EOB source also contains it.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/claim/structuredefinition-Claim.xml already contains the exact requested definition, and the checked Claim SVG tooltip is consistent with the authoritative XML source.

related_jiras.note: Published EOB issue requested the same prescription definition for ExplanationOfBenefit.prescription and is already reflected in current EOB source; it was not separately decided in this seed run.
